title: Virus Cryopreservation Protocol
protocol: Follow the laboratory protocol for viral growth and purification.
Maintain non-enveloped viruses and some DNA viruses at 4°C for long-term storage.
Store RNA and most enveloped viruses by snap-freezing and keeping them at -80°C.
Place the viral preparation in a reagent reservoir on a thermo-conductive CoolSink BX50 module for cooling.
Alternatively, rest the CoolSink on a ThermalTray LP platform in an ice pan to minimize contact with ice.
Dispense 1 ml of virus preparation into a pre-labeled TruCool cryovial.
Maintain vials at 4°C in a CoolBox CFT30 ice-free cooling station.
Place a second CoolRack CFT30 module on dry-ice and let it equilibrate to -78°C for five to ten minutes.
Place the cryo vials directly into the pre-equilibrated CoolRack CFT30 wells to snap-freeze the samples.
Transfer frozen samples to a storage box.
Store the storage box in the -80°C freezer for long-term storage.
Transfer cryo vials from the -80°C freezer into a pre-equilibrated CoolBox CFT30 containing a green freezing cartridge.
Place the vials directly in a 37°C water bath and manually agitate to enable thawing.
Remove the vial from the 37°C water bath once the liquid is almost completely thawed.
Place the vial on a CoolRack CFT30 that has been previously equilibrated on ice.
Samples are now ready for desired experimental procedures or titer assessment.
